messages:
sam: paging — seeing a sharp perf cliff in continuous-batching at ~1300 concurrent requests. 95p latency jumped from ~120ms to >2s and error 500s on cb-worker pods. KV cache size climbed to 98% and eviction storms started. tagging @maria @alex
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 (severity: S2) — paging eng-oncall, runbook: continuous-batching-perf
maria: ack — pulling metrics now. which customer is hitting this? any recent deploys?
sam: no deploys in past 25m, rolling traffic bump from a partner integration at 13:04 UTC. load graphs: https://grafana/redwood/d/CB/continuous-batch?from=-30m to now
alex: I see microbatch queues saturating. queue_length and queue_wait_time correlate with increased KV cache fetches. hypothesis: concurrent microbatches cause repeated KV cache cold lookups because prefix cache misses cascade.
jamie: can we temporarily throttle concurrency and reduce max_microbatch_tokens? doing so helped on previous KV blowups.
maria: agreed. I'll push a config override to staging then prod. patch: ```
# runtime config override
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  max_microbatch_tokens: 256   # was 1024
  max_concurrent_microbatches: 48  # was 200
  microbatch_jitter_ms: 35
  kv_cache_ttl_sec: 2
```

maria: sending canary to 3 pods now (cb-canary-1..3). watch latency and error rate for 2 min, rolling if green.
oncall-bot: Deploy started by maria (canary): config-override/continuous-batch-180612-1
sam: observed immediate drop in queue_wait_time on canaries, KV cache E2E latency down ~60% on those hosts. errors small sample still at 1.2% overall.
alex: also enabling prefix-KV caching amplification cap as a mitigation: `kv_cache.max_prefetch = 4`. This should limit cascade. I'll apply to canary only.
jamie: i'm throttling the tenant route for the partner to 30rps at the edge to reduce incoming concurrency.
maria: canary looks stable for 5m. starting progressive rollout to remaining pods with 30s stagger.
sam: customers impacted: 4 partners reported slow responses (timeout retries) between 13:02-13:20 UTC — SLO breaches for 3 tenants. CS notified and posting status update.
jamie: status update drafted for status.redwood: "Investigating intermittent high latency on text generation routes. Mitigation in progress: reducing batching concurrency, applying jitter and cache caps."
maria: rollout complete at 13:30 UTC. post-rollout metrics: 95p down to 140ms, error rate back to baseline. KV cache memory stable ~45%.
sam: notes for postmortem: root cause likely interaction of sudden concurrency spike + high max_microbatch_tokens causing huge cache churn and synchronous fetch storms. fixes: (1) conservative defaults for max_microbatch_tokens (2) enforce microbatch jitter by default (3) hard limit on concurrent_microbatches per worker (4) add circuit breaker to KV cache fetch fanout.
oncall-bot: Handoff reminder — maria is primary until 15:00 UTC, then alex takes over.
maria: adding runbook patch and playbook steps to repo: https://git.internal/redwood/runbooks/continuous-batching.md#kv-cache-blowup
jamie: assigning follow-ups: @alex to add automated canary for config changes, @sam to own customer-impact timeline, @maria to write postmortem.
sam: leaving handoff notes for next oncall: if latency climbs again, first action: reduce `max_concurrent_microbatches` to 32 and throttle ingress to affected tenant, then escalate to on-call-sre.
alex: +1. also recommend alert tuning: add a "KV cache eviction-rate" alert with short window to catch blowups earlier.
maria: thanks team. unlocking incident, will mark as resolved once PM & CS ack postmortem items."
